questions.scenario: A company must keep its customer database on-premises for compliance, but wants to host its public website in Azure and let the website read from that database.
questions.question: Which cloud model is this?

options.why: Part of the solution remains on-premises, so it is not purely public.
The website runs in a public cloud, so it is not purely private.
Correct. On-premises and public cloud are combined and connected.
Multi-cloud means multiple public cloud providers.

questions.explanation: Combining on-premises infrastructure with public cloud, connected so they work together, is hybrid cloud.

questions.question: An organisation uses both Microsoft Azure and another public cloud provider. What is this approach called?

options.why: Correct. Using more than one public cloud provider is multi-cloud.
Private cloud is dedicated infrastructure for one organisation.
Serverless is a compute model, not a provider strategy.

questions.explanation: Multi-cloud = two or more public cloud providers.

questions.question: Which Azure service lets you manage on-premises servers and servers in other clouds with Azure tools such as Azure Policy?

options.why: Correct. Arc extends Azure management to resources outside Azure.
Advisor recommends optimisations for Azure resources.
Data Box is for offline data transfer.

questions.explanation: Azure Arc projects external servers, Kubernetes clusters and data services into Azure for unified management and governance.

questions.question: Which TWO are benefits of a hybrid cloud?

options.text: Sensitive workloads can stay on-premises while others use the public cloud
options.why: Correct. Flexibility of placement is the core benefit.

options.text: It removes all on-premises hardware costs
options.why: On-premises parts still have hardware costs.

options.text: Extra capacity can be used in the cloud during demand peaks
It is always simpler to manage than a single cloud

questions.explanation: Hybrid offers workload placement flexibility and burst capacity, at the cost of extra complexity.
